title: Trial hears how RCMP sniper killed suspect
article: An RCMP sniper shot and killed one of three suspects who had fled after the murder of Const. Dennis Strongquill in Manitoba last December, a trial was told Tuesday.
Killed was Danny Sand, the brother of Robert Marlo Sand, 23, who is on trial for first-degree murder with Laurie Ann Bell, 20.
They are charged in the shooting death of Strongquill, 52, in December 2001. It is the second day of the trial.
The shooting of Strongquill happened outside Russell, Man. The RCMP caught up with the three suspects about 14 hours later at a motel in Wolseley, Sask., about 200 kilometres west of Russell.
Const. Bob Gourlay was the spotter for the RCMP sniper. He testified that he heard gunshots at the motel, then saw Sand on the roof loading a rifle. The sniper shot and killed Sand.
Under cross-examination, Gourlay admitted he didn't know who fired the earlier shots and that Danny Sand was not pointing the rifle at police.
"I felt he had the capability of killing someone with that rifle he had in his hands," Gourlay said.
Other members of the RCMP sniper team are expected to testify.
The Crown alleges that the Sand brothers and Bell were engaged in a crime spree prior to their encounter with Strongquill, who was shot after his cruiser was rammed as part of a chase.
The trial is expected to last 10 weeks.
